<thought>We will search for templates that break a halide and form a primary amine (SNAr). Use the target molecule as one of the precursors? Actually the search expects target molecule SMILES. We can use the sulfonyl chloride aromatic with F as target? But the template applied to product yields that precursor. The target molecule is the product (diaryl amine). However we don't have its SMILES. Could we use the first precursor as target? The template would break C-F and form C-N, so the product would be the amine attached to aromatic. That's the product we need. So we can use the product SMILES approximated as O=S(Cl)(=O)C1=CC(Nc2ccc3c(c2)C(CCC4(CCC4)O4)=C(N5CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC5)C2=CC=CC=C2)=CC=C1 (without extra parentheses). Let's try that simpler version: O=S(Cl)(=O)C1=CC(Nc2ccc3c(c2)C(CCC4(CCC4)O4)=C(N5CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC5)C2=CC=CC=C2)=CC=C1

We'll search with broken "aryl halide" and formed "secondary amines"? Actually the product has secondary amine (N attached to two aryl groups). So functional_groups_formed: ["secondary amines"].
